revision_history.author: project_manager
revision_history.description: Risk register authored because MAN.5 was recorded as a coverage gap. This is project risk to the development, not a threat assessment: the cybersecurity TARA FB2-SAF-TAR-000001 is a different artifact with a different subject matter and does not satisfy MAN.5.

risk_entries.cause: The margin was entered as a wish rather than as the difference between the interval and the work. Nothing in the process checked the sum.
risk_entries.effect_on_the_project: A baselined record cannot be corrected without a controlled change, so the project either carries a known-invalid budget or opens a change against a baselined safety goal.

mitigation_actions.action: Raise a finding recording the arithmetic rather than editing the safety goal
mitigation_actions.evidence_of_effect: Finding FB2-REV-FND-000025 records the arithmetic. The technical safety concept FB2-SAF-TSC-000001 now carries a budget that closes and names the departure.

mitigation_actions.action: Open a controlled change against FB2-SAF-SGO-000001 to reconcile the recorded margin with the interval
mitigation_actions.evidence_of_effect: Not yet opened. The change record does not exist.

risk_entries.residual_exposure_argument: The contradiction is now visible and owned. The residual exposure is the time until the change is opened and the gate cannot pass until it is.

risk_statement.condition: The 100 ms fault-tolerant time interval is spent by a budget whose serial elements sum to 85 ms and whose recorded margin is 20 ms
risk_statement.consequence: The safety goal is baselined with an arithmetic that does not close, and every requirement and measure derived from it inherits an unachievable budget

risk_entries.title: The safety goal's timing budget does not close
risk_entries.trigger_for_escalation: Any requirement or measure raised against this safety goal before the change is closed.

risk_entries.cause: Competence planning named one holder per specialism and no deputy, because building a second qualified reviewer was not funded.
risk_entries.effect_on_the_project: Gate dates slip on absence, as the progress record for 2026-03-06 shows, and the slip is not recoverable because no one else can perform the review.

mitigation_actions.action: Name and fund a deputy for each single-holder specialism
mitigation_actions.evidence_of_effect: Not done. The register still shows four single points of failure in the plan's resource table.

risk_entries.residual_exposure_argument: No action has been taken, so the residual exposure equals the inherent exposure. Recording it as equal is more useful than recording an improvement that did not happen.

risk_statement.condition: Only one person in the fictional programme is qualified to review severity and controllability reasoning and to approve a safety concept
risk_statement.consequence: Every safety gate depends on one person's calendar, and a review queue forms behind a single absence

risk_entries.title: Single qualified reviewer for the safety reasoning
risk_entries.trigger_for_escalation: Any absence of the single holder exceeding five working days.

risk_entries.cause: The corpus was authored by an automated process with no access to a human review organisation, and no independent reviewer was ever engaged.
risk_entries.effect_on_the_project: The safety case cannot be assembled at all. This is not a schedule risk; it is a risk that the project's central deliverable cannot be produced.

mitigation_actions.action: Record the absence as an explicit limitation on every review record rather than letting the review count imply independence
mitigation_actions.evidence_of_effect: Every review record in the corpus carries a limitations entry stating that the review is automated and is not human confirmation.
Not engaged. Nothing in this corpus can stand in for it.

risk_entries.residual_exposure_argument: Mitigating the impact by documenting it does not reduce the exposure. The project's deliverable cannot exist until a real reviewer is engaged, and that is outside what an automated process can do.

risk_statement.condition: Every review record in the corpus is an automated AI review performed in a coding-agent session
risk_statement.consequence: No review in the corpus has organisational independence, which an ASIL D safety case requires and which master-prompt clause 2.9 says an AI review is not

risk_entries.title: No independent confirmation reviewer exists
risk_entries.trigger_for_escalation: Any statement anywhere in the corpus that implies a reviewed or approved state without naming this limitation.

risk_entries.cause: The plan funded writing measures and did not fund building the benches, the bus injection nodes, the network capture points or the vehicle. The 2026-11-06 progress record shows the plan did not fund them.
risk_entries.effect_on_the_project: The verification-readiness gate cannot pass, so the release gate cannot pass, so the project cannot ship. Nine measures are affected and none can be executed by any means available to this corpus.

mitigation_actions.action: Record each blocked execution with the reason and the specific condition that would unblock it
mitigation_actions.evidence_of_effect: All nine new execution records carry execution_kind 'none' and outcome 'blocked' with a what_would_unblock_it list.
Not funded. No budget line exists.

risk_entries.residual_exposure_argument: Honest recording of a blocked execution does not make the project able to proceed. It only makes the blocker impossible to overlook.

risk_statement.condition: Verification measures are written but no execution environment exists for the security, validation or hardware-injection measures
risk_statement.consequence: Every requirement whose measure needs an environment ends the project with an unexecuted plan and a blocked execution record

risk_entries.title: Verification harnesses are unfunded
risk_entries.trigger_for_escalation: Any planning cycle that treats the verification measures as covered because they exist.

risk_entries.cause: The hypothetical programme assumed a supplier monitoring process would be established during procurement. It has not been.
risk_entries.effect_on_the_project: The safety argument's assumption that components meet their specification has no monitoring behind it, and the third-party-component half of FB2-SAF-SEC-000005 cannot be satisfied.

mitigation_actions.action: Define the supplier monitoring process and record it
mitigation_actions.evidence_of_effect: Process record FB2-SUP-SPL-000001 defines ACQ.4 with its inputs, outputs, acceptance criteria and one performed instance.

mitigation_actions.action: Establish the contractual means to obtain component change notification

risk_entries.residual_exposure_argument: A defined process with one recorded instance is better than no process, but a process with no contractual hook cannot be executed against a supplier who is not obliged to respond.

risk_statement.condition: The item depends on an analogue front end, a safe base controller, a current sensor and a memory device, all from named vendors, none of which is under any monitoring relationship
risk_statement.consequence: A component changes behaviour, or an advisory appears against it, and the project has no contractual or technical means of finding out before a vehicle ships

risk_entries.title: Supplier monitoring has no accountable supplier
risk_entries.trigger_for_escalation: Any advisory published against any component in the item.

risk_entries.cause: The requirements were authored from the safety goal without the intermediate system requirements that would have decomposed it, so the hardware record was written at the same level as the functional record and in the same words.
risk_entries.effect_on_the_project: A duplicated obligation at two levels is invisible to a link check because both endpoints resolve. It is only visible on read, which is why it was found while writing the technical safety concept.

mitigation_actions.action: Raise a finding recording the duplication instead of editing either record
mitigation_actions.evidence_of_effect: Finding FB2-REV-FND-000027 records the verbatim duplication between FB2-SAF-FSR-000004 and FB2-HW-TSR-000004.

mitigation_actions.action: Decompose the functional requirement into distinct technical statements
mitigation_actions.evidence_of_effect: Not done. Both records remain as they were.

risk_entries.residual_exposure_argument: The finding makes the problem visible to a reviewer but leaves the corpus with the duplication until the change is raised.

risk_statement.condition: Technical safety requirements exist at both the functional and the hardware level with identical text
risk_statement.consequence: Two records at two different ISO 26262 levels claim the same obligation, so neither can be reviewed as a decomposition and the reader cannot tell which is authoritative

risk_entries.title: Requirement and concept records are authored before the derivation that would justify them
risk_entries.trigger_for_escalation: Any third record appearing with the same statement text.

risk_entries.cause: The corpus was built bottom-up from the cell-voltage safety chain, and that chain stops at the reaction. Nothing forced the lifecycle after it to exist.
risk_entries.effect_on_the_project: ISO 26262 Part 7 is entirely unsatisfied and the release-readiness gate cannot pass on its lifecycle criteria.

mitigation_actions.action: Author a post-development record for each of the six areas
mitigation_actions.evidence_of_effect: FB2-REL-RLS-000001, FB2-PRD-EOL-000001, FB2-PRD-CAL-000001, FB2-OPS-MON-000001, FB2-SVC-SVC-000001 and FB2-DEC-DCM-000001 now exist and each states that none of its steps has been executed.

mitigation_actions.action: Obtain the organisational capability to execute them
mitigation_actions.evidence_of_effect: Not obtained. There is no plant, no line and no service organisation.

risk_entries.residual_exposure_argument: The likelihood fell because the areas are now documented and the likelihood that a reader believes they are operational fell. The impact did not move at all.

risk_statement.condition: Release identification, production and end-of-line test, calibration, field monitoring, service and decommissioning are all unpopulated
risk_statement.consequence: A configuration could ship without being identified, a pack could leave the line without being tested, and an energised pack could be handled by a party that does not know it is energised

risk_entries.title: Incomplete post-development lifecycle
risk_entries.trigger_for_escalation: Any external party treating one of these records as an authorised procedure.

risk_entries.cause: Reuse was treated as a listing exercise rather than as an assurance decision.
risk_entries.effect_on_the_project: The freedom-from-interference argument for the software layer rests on an unexamined assumption about what the reused code is permitted to do.

mitigation_actions.action: Define the reuse process with an assessment per reused element
mitigation_actions.evidence_of_effect: Process record FB2-SUP-RUS-000001 defines REU.2 with its acceptance criteria and one performed instance.

mitigation_actions.action: Complete a reuse assessment for every element on a safety path
mitigation_actions.evidence_of_effect: Not done. No assessment record exists.

risk_entries.residual_exposure_argument: Defining the process does not assess anything. The residual exposure is unchanged.

risk_statement.condition: The reference implementation reuses an operating system, driver code from several vendors and generated code, and the corpus holds a reuse inventory but no reuse assessment
risk_statement.consequence: Code runs on a safety path whose provenance, qualification status and modification constraints are unknown

risk_entries.title: Reused and generated code assurance is not established
risk_entries.trigger_for_escalation: Any safety-path requirement whose allocation depends on a reused element with no assessment.

record_verbatim.scope_note: This register covers risk to the development of the hypothetical programme: schedule, resource, technical, supplier, quality, tooling, compliance and organisational risk. It does NOT cover risk arising from the product's behaviour in service, which the cybersecurity TARA FB2-SAF-TAR-000001 and the hazard analysis FB2-SAF-HAZ-000001 address, and it does not cover functional-safety hazard risk, which the safety analyses address. The three are separate registers with separate acceptance authorities in a real programme, and conflating them would let a product risk be accepted by a project manager.

scoring_method.escalation_threshold: high/major and high/moderate escalate to the safety manager at the next fortnightly review. medium/major escalates to the project manager's sponsor, which in this fictional programme is the safety manager. Every other pair is managed at review.
scoring_method.exposure_formula: Exposure is the ordinal pair (probability, impact), written as e.g. 'high/moderate'. It is deliberately NOT a product of two label scores multiplied together: the labels have no numeric meaning, so a product would be a number with no derivation behind it. Escalation is on the pair, not on a total.

impact_scale.definition: Absorbed inside the package's float; no gate moved.
impact_scale.label: minor

impact_scale.definition: A gate moves; a package needs rework; float is consumed.
impact_scale.label: moderate

impact_scale.definition: A gate criterion cannot be met as written, or a safety or compliance record must be reopened.
impact_scale.label: major

probability_scale.definition: Not expected within the planned programme duration; would require an unusual combination of circumstances.
probability_scale.label: low

probability_scale.definition: Could occur once within the planned programme duration.
probability_scale.label: medium

probability_scale.definition: Expected to occur at least once, or already has.
probability_scale.label: high

4. date - ISO-8601, checked by grammar and by parse

5. review_packet{path, sha256, record_sha256_at_signing}; path must resolve to a packet.json on disk under docs/artifacts/reviews/signed ONLY - the regenerated tree docs/artifacts/reviews/packets is NOT admissible, because it is rewritten on every regeneration and would destroy your evidence; sha256 must equal that file's bytes now; record_sha256_at_signing must equal this packet's integrity.record_sha256; target.record_id and target.profile must both name this record

6. approval_ledger_ref{ledger_id, entry_sha256} naming your entry in docs/artifacts/governance/approval-ledger.jsonl. It is approval METADATA, not content: it is excluded from the record's content digest and is never a revision_history entry, so recording it neither bumps the revision nor stales a link. signature_block._packet_sha256_note: The digest of this packet.json's own bytes. It is deliberately left null rather than filled, because a file cannot contain its own digest. Compute it with `shasum -a 256`, or use `--transcribe`, which resolves it.
signature_block._recording: Archive the signed packet under docs/artifacts/reviews/signed/<profile>/<id>.json, then record the approval as human_approval_status plus an approval_evidence.human_approval block on the record, plus approval_ledger_ref naming one appended line in docs/artifacts/governance/approval-ledger.jsonl. Do NOT add a revision_history entry: see docs/artifacts/governance/approval-ledger.md.
signature_block._rule: Empty by construction. No automated process may fill this. Filling it in is the only thing that changes human_approval_status on the record. As of 2026-10-04 (amendment APPROVAL-RULE-A1) the corpus rule human_approval_rejected is an EVIDENCE requirement, not a prohibition: a properly evidenced approval is ACCEPTED and keeps `corpus.py check` green, while a bare grant value is still rejected. What the validator reads is contract.approval_evidence_block below; it fails if any of its six elements is missing, and the finding names which.

signature_policy: The signature block below is empty by construction. This tool has no code path that writes a decision, an approval, a signature or an execution verdict. Filling it is a human action. As of 2026-10-04 (amendment APPROVAL-RULE-A1) the corpus ACCEPTS a properly evidenced approval rather than banning the value outright, so this rule now has to carry the evidence contract in full: see signature_block._contract. Since the same day (amendment APPROVAL-LEDGER-A1) the approval is recorded in the append-only ledger at docs/artifacts/governance/approval-ledger.jsonl and the record keeps only a reference to it, so recording your signature neither bumps the revision nor invalidates any review digest.
